newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra to unveil A$3 bln div today-paper.
newsitem.headline: Telstra to unveil A$3 bln div today-paper.

text.p: Australian state-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp would announce the payment of a special A$3 billion dividend to the government on Friday, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported.
Telstra officials refused to comment on reports of the special dividend earlier this week.

But the Financial Review said an announcement of the dividend, to be funded by borrowing, was expected on Friday morning. The Liberal-National government plans to sell one-third of the carrier by the end of calendar 1997.

"The government considers the dividend payment to be a bringing forward of proceeds it would have got from the sale of Telstra if it had been sold with a 'lazy' balance sheet, with minimal debt," the newspaper said.
The payment was agreed by Telstra's board on Thursday and would be made within the fiscal year to June 30, 1997, it said.

But it would not help the government rein in its underlying budget deficit, which excludes asset sales and state government debt repayment. The underlying deficit is projected at A$8.5 billion in 1996/97.
Treasurer Peter Costello is due to release the 1997/98 budget on May 13.
